10.0.0.en: 1 And the king Ahasuerus laid a tribute upon the land and upon the isles of the sea. 2 And all the acts of his power and of his might, and the declaration of the greatness of Mordecai, whereunto the king advanced him, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Media and Persia? 3 For Mordecai the Jew was next unto king Ahasuerus, and great among the Jews, and accepted of the multitude of his brethren, seeking the good of his people and speaking peace to all his seed.

10.1.0.en: This chapter presented to us a picture of the greatness of Ahasuerus, to whom many provinces submitted, offering him tribute, and the second man was Mordecai, “great among the Jews and accepted of the multitude of his brethren, seeking the good of his people and speaking peace to all his seed” [3]. The secret of his greatness was the breadth of his heart with love for his brethren, and his speaking of peace for the sake of his children. He became a secret of blessing for his generation and for generations to come through his surpassing love.

10.1.1.en: If the whole people were glorified by their salvation from the enemy, then Mordecai, who sought not his own things but those of others, was glorified more and more.

10.1.2.en: And in the Additions to Esther, this chapter continues with a review of Mordecai's dream, in which God assured him that He was working through him and Esther for the salvation of their brethren, and we have previously spoken of this dream.

10.1.3.en: Our good God, who gave Esther and Mordecai the grace of an open mouth and a heart broadened with love for their brethren, opens our hearts for the edification of every soul, to the glory of God!

10.1.4.en: * You will find the interpretations of the remaining chapters of the book in Fr. Antonious Fekry's commentary on the Book of Esther.
